intended_object: A coherence isomorphism e(e^{j-1}(Y)) ≅ e^j(Y) for an autoequivalence e of C. It is built from the canonical identification e^{j-1}·e ≅ e^j and a transport along the integer equality j-1+1 = j. I inferred this from the docstring and the body; the library uses it in its graded Ext / Euler characteristic shift machinery.
explanation: This is an auxiliary device, not a mathematical object. It is a canonical comparison isomorphism needed only because, in Lean, the object e^{j-1+1}(Y) is not definitionally equal to e^j(Y). Mathematically, it is the obvious identification e ∘ e^{j-1} ≅ e^j, which is the identity up to coherence. It is defined by composing the inverse of `powSuccRightIso (j-1)` at Y with an `eqToIso` coming from j - 1 + 1 = j. So it is bookkeeping for moving a source shift into the internal degree when working with graded Ext. It has no standalone counterpart in the literature that it could fail to formalize.
